summary: Traffic hotspot causes accept-queue skew and api-gateway priority-aging, triggering upstream runtime exit loop and 5xx surge
description:
Issue summary:
A dedicated-customer tenant (NimbusHealth) experienced a sudden and sustained rise in 5xx errors on several streaming and embedding routes beginning ~2026-03-10T08:50Z. Error rate for the tenant rose from baseline ~0.3% to a peak of ~8% over a 20-minute window and remained elevated during the afternoon.

Impact:
- Customer-facing requests returned 5xx at scale (502/503/504 mix) causing degraded UX for NimbusHealth users.
- Throughput for the tenant reduced by ~45% when customer applied client-side throttles.
- No broad region-wide outage; issue scoped to routes serving this tenant weight in us-east-1.

Environment:
- Prod cluster: us-east-1 (apigw fleet + serving-runtime dedicated pool for tenant).
- Customer tier: dedicated (tenant pinned to dedicated route weights).
- Affected model variants: redwood-7b-instruct, owl-13b-v1 (both used by different endpoints).

Steps to reproduce / observed sequence:
1) Tenant produced a traffic hotspot when a scheduled batch of embedding uploads and long-chat sessions overlapped (customer-provided timestamps attached).
2) apigw accept_queue depth grows on a subset of replicas. Backpressure and priority-windowing cause head-of-line delay for some streaming connections.
3) Long-lived requests start accumulating at the apigw layer and are delivered to runtimes in bursts; runtime prefetch/kvcache churn increases.
4) Several runtime pods report repeated process exits (exit code 137) and rapid restarts; NVML logs show transient GPU driver resets for the same pods.
5) The apigw surfaces 502/503 responses while retries and hedged requests amplify the fanout, sustaining elevated 5xx rate.

Logs & metrics (snippets):
- apigw metrics: accept_queue_depth(nimbus-tenant) = 178 -> 0 over 18m window; p50 latency jump 85ms -> 420ms; 5xx rate: 0.3% -> 8.1%
- runtime logs (pod runtime-xyz-7): "SIGKILL: out of memory" followed by "process exited with status 137" at 2026-03-10T09:06:14Z
- nvml: "GPU 0: reset due to unknown error" x 3 in 5m interval
- sample request ids: rq_20260310_090601_az1 (attached)

Initial hypothesis:
- Not a pure GPU OOM from model weights alone; pattern looks like head-of-line blocking at apigw (priority-window aging) causing request bursts to reach runtime while KV cache/prefetch is in heavy churn -> memory pressure and driver resets leading to exits.
- Hedged retries from the client and apigw retry heuristics amplified the load on runtimes.

Immediate mitigation taken / proposed:
- Short-term: customer applied client-side concurrency throttle (25% of normal) which reduced 5xx but also reduced throughput.
- SRE action: moved NimbusHealth to an isolated route weight group (reduce cross-tenant interference) and temporarily raised runtime prefetch limits to reduce eviction churn.
- Applied apigw config tweak to lower hedged-retry amplification for the tenant for 6 hours.

Next steps (planned):
- 1) Collect a full set of core dumps and GPU driver logs from affected runtime instances for deeper analysis.
- 2) Run a controlled replay of the customer's request pattern in staging to reproduce accept-queue skew and eviction behavior.
- 3) Add telemetry for per-tenant priority-window age and head-of-line wait times in apigw dashboards.
- 4) Consider long-term: route isolation by default for high-concurrency tenants and smarter hedged-retry backoff.

Workaround for customer:
- Keep concurrency cap at 25% for next 24-36 hours OR shift heavy batch uploads to off-peak windows. SRE recommends using the smaller embedding batch size while we stabilize.

Request from customer:
- ETA for a permanent fix and whether Redwood can proactively schedule a dedicated prewarm window to avoid future accept-queue storms.

resolution_notes: Mitigation deployed 2026-03-12 14:30: isolated route weight + prefetch limit increase + hedged-retry dampening. Observed tenant 5xx rate reduce from ~6.8% to ~0.4% within 2 hours. Next actions: capture runtime cores, run replay test in staging, update apigw dashboards for priority-window age, and schedule a 72-hour monitoring window. Postmortem to be authored after 72h stability window.
root_cause_summary: Accept-queue priority-aging at the API gateway combined with a tenant traffic hotspot led to head-of-line blocking. That produced bursty delivery patterns to runtimes, increasing KV cache/prefetch churn and memory pressure which precipitated runtime process exits (driver resets) and a cascade of 5xx responses.
